description: Sequential switch sending whichever of eight inputs is currently selected to a single output, stepping forwards, backwards, at random or by an addressing voltage

params.text: Sets how many of the eight inputs are stepped through, from 1 to 8
Picks forward, pendulum, reverse, random or voltage addressed stepping, shown by the coloured lamps
In voltage addressed stepping, picks which input is selected, read at each clock edge; with a cable in the address CV input it attenuates that voltage instead
Chooses how the output behaves: S&H holds the value sampled as each input was selected, the arrow passes the selected input straight through, T&H holds the last value that passed

inputs.text: A high gate lets the switch step on and a low gate holds it where it is, stepping resuming at the next clock; with nothing patched here the switch always runs
Each rising edge moves the selection on by one step; any signal crossing 2V counts as a high gate
A rising edge sends the selection back to input one on the next clock, and until that clock arrives the output is held at 0V
Sets how many of the eight inputs are stepped through, 10V giving all eight, and takes the LENGTH knob out of circuit
Sets the stepping pattern by voltage and takes the DIRECTION knob out of circuit: under 1V forward, 1V to 2V pendulum, 2V to 3V reverse, 3V to 4V random, 4V and over voltage addressed
In voltage addressed stepping this voltage picks the input, 0-10V covering the whole set length whatever it is, with the ADDR knob attenuating it
Routed to the output while that step is the selected one; all channels of a polyphonic cable are carried through

outputs.text: Carries the signal from whichever input is currently selected, behaving as MODE is set

inputs.0: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.2: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
